Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-boost-slack-medium-0041", "row_sha256": "6830dd7340c609cc5d6fb2a0f7eaf929cf2b5210ba7e7cec3ecc6327d9c71cbe", "mode": "/slack", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Fix grammar, punctuation, and shorthand with minimal edits. Keep casual tone, contractions, emoji, and the original request. Return correct text unchanged.", "input": "hey folks, could we update the log cleanup utility before friday? right now it scans the shared folder every night, and i'm not sure it handles the archive check the way we need. for this run, please have it delete a local log only if it's older than 30 days and has a matching copy in the nightly S3 archive. if either of those checks fails, don't delete the file; leave it where it is and add its path to the review report instead. that way we can catch older logs that didn't make it into the archive, plus newer ones that are still in use. could the report include the file's age and whether the archive copy was found? no need to change how the utility names the report or where it saves it. also, let's keep the current folder scan and schedule as-is, since the ops team already relies on those. if this is a small change, it'd be great to get it into the friday run; otherwise, just let me know what needs to move. thanks!", "output": "Hey folks, could we update the log cleanup utility before Friday? Right now, it scans the shared folder every night, and I'm not sure it handles the archive check the way we need. For this run, please have it delete a local log only if it's older than 30 days and has a matching copy in the nightly S3 archive. If either of those checks fails, don't delete the file; leave it where it is and add its path to the review report instead. That way, we can catch older logs that didn't make it into the archive, plus newer ones that are still in use. Could the report include the file's age and whether the archive copy was found? No need to change how the utility names the report or where it saves it. Also, let's keep the current folder scan and schedule as-is, since the ops team already relies on those. If this is a small change, it'd be great to get it into the Friday run; otherwise, just let me know what needs to move. Thanks!"}]
